title: Electoral Legislation Amendment (Fair and Transparent Elections) Bill 2024 (No. 2)
short_title: Electoral Legislation Amendment (Fair and Transparent Elections) Bill 2024 (No. 2)

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 and related legislation to tighten donation disclosure, restrict some donations and government advertising, and increase territory Senate representation.
It would lower the donation disclosure threshold from $16,300 to a fixed $1,000 and require recipients to disclose gifts within 7 days of the threshold being exceeded.

It would also bar donations from tobacco, fossil fuel, gambling and liquor businesses and substantial Commonwealth contractors and bidders, and give the Australian Capital Territory and the Northern Territory half a state's senators.
changes: A person's contributions over an election cycle would be capped at 2 per cent of public funding at the previous election, with offences for exceeding it.

Printing, publishing or distributing electoral or referendum matter containing a statement of fact that is misleading or deceptive to a material extent would become an offence, with investigation powers for the Electoral Commissioner.
The definition of a gift would widen to cover fundraising dinners, paid business forums and other events, and membership fees benefiting a political entity or candidate.

Independent candidates could register an independent campaign entity, nominated by at least 100 electors, to be treated like a registered political party for electoral roll access and disclosure deadlines.
Government advertising would be prohibited from 2 years after a general election until the next election, unless the Independent Communications Committee determines it exempt.
summary.affected: Political parties, candidates, donors, tobacco, fossil fuel, gambling and liquor businesses, substantial Commonwealth contractors and bidders, independent candidates and territory voters are affected.
